subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking questions & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking questions & next steps

Hi Jane -

Great to speak earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call regarding Acme's Private VPC deployment: 

1) Goal: Run Redwood Private (VPC deployment) behind Acme's network controls for regulatory data handling.
2) Recommended topology: VPC peering for low-latency intra-region traffic OR AWS PrivateLink if you prefer managed endpoints and tighter control over inbound IPs. We recommended PrivateLink for your multi-account setup, but are flexible.
3) Network items we need from your side:
   - CIDR ranges for the VPCs that will connect to Redwood (preferred: primary and secondary ranges)
   - Any egress firewall rules / IP allowlist requirements (we can provide a short list of Redwood egress IPs if you need them)
   - Preferred connectivity pattern: VPC peering or PrivateLink

Next steps:
- Can your networking/security lead share the CIDR ranges and whether you want PrivateLink or peering?
- Sean (cc'd) can run the technical session to go over routing, NAT, and IP allowlist details - are M/W/F next week good for a 60-min call?
- I'll start a procurement thread with pricing & draft SOW once we have the deployment topology.

Attaching our Private VPC checklist to make the network ask as simple as possible. Happy to jump on a call this week if easier.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>, Mike Lee <mike.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment follow-up: networking questions & next steps

Hi Jane / Mike -

Thanks for the details and the CIDR sheet. Confirming a few technical points and what I'll cover on the technical call:

1) PrivateLink is a solid choice for multi-account setups and reduces the blast radius compared to wide VPC peering. We'll walk through the VPC endpoint creation flow (Interface endpoints) and required IAM permissions for your account admins.

2) CIDRs noted: 10.20.0.0/16 (prod), 10.21.0.0/16 (staging). Please confirm if these are the EGRESS ranges or the VPC internal ranges. If you use NAT for outbound, we need the NAT/public IPs for allowlisting. If not, we'll provide the Redwood side PrivateLink endpoint DNS names which you can secure via your internal DNS.

3) IP allowlist: For PrivateLink you can restrict by security group and inline ACLs. If you need IP-level allowlist (e.g., for on-prem firewalls), provide the NAT public IPs and we'll map them to the minimal set of egress addresses. Typical setup:
   - Create Interface Endpoint in each account/subnet that needs access
   - Update route tables/security groups to allow outbound to the endpoint
   - If you need IP-based filtering at the perimeter, allow Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide a short list)

4) Required permissions for your AWS admin during setup (we'll share an exact policy doc on the call).

I can run the technical call on Wed 7/28 at 9:30am PT or Thu 7/29 at 9:00am PT - which works better for you? I'll prepare a short slide deck and the specific CLI steps for your network team.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
